author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
Why does everyone think AI writing bad code is a problem?

We have natural un-intelligence writing bad code day in day out for decades, and we are mostly doing fine.

comments.text:
A lot of the aggressive AI criticism on this platform isn't about technical accuracy—it's about job security.

When a technology threatens to automate routine tasks people built their careers on, instinct kicks in:

- Label it useless.
- Magnify every mistake.
- Hope it goes away.

Dismissing AI might buy short-term peace of mind, but it won't stop the industry from evolving.

author.name: Martin Zouhar
author.headline: Scientific Researcher/Programmer at Institute of Scientific Instruments of the CAS

comments.text:
How about the following:

Because if you review what you perceive to be a smelly code and the committer replies "LLM told me so" without having a good defence why it should be this way OR admit "I messed up by blindly trusting and not checking thoroughly." it simply... makes you, let's put it mildly, upset.

And if many companies claim to be *all* for carbon neutrality accepting sub-optimal code from AI/LLM (because it can just be a minimal viable product) instead of hiring capable people and giving them the time to do it right (I am not against LLM's assistence), they increase electricity consumption shooting themselves in their hypocritical feet.
